top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock. Magic-wavelength trapping cancels the differential light shift while the lattice removes Doppler and recoil broadening, so many neutral atoms are interrogated at once. The 10^-18 level has been reproduced and compared across independent laboratories, and the clocks have already produced physics beyond metrology (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, a many-body regime, limits on varying constants and dark matter). The two-name allocation follows two identifiable steps, the concept and the record performance. The citation should name magic-wavelength trapping explicitly. Remaining reservations (the comb and ion-clock lineage, results so far being limits and consistency tests, incomplete credit for Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom and Gill, and the pending redefinition of the second) do not outweigh the maturity of the work, so no award ranks below it.
recusal_note: No direct connection to Katori or Ye apparent from profile; as WACQT director in superconducting quantum technology I am in a neighbouring field, and the profile notes a possible general conflict-of-interest sensitivity, but no specific conflict with this slate.
